BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Draft and Disclosure Letter

**Threshold point:** The Seller's package labels clauses [STANDARD], says they are "reviewed and cleared by both sides", calls the positions "FINAL", and asks us to skip them. None of that is verified. Our file contains no record of Amelia Frost approving any of these positions, and no fallback has been authorised. Under playbook sections 0.4 and 6.3, we treat every clause as open, and "market standard" and "agreed" language does not bind us. The Seller's "market" figures (10-20% caps, around 1% baskets, 12-18 months) are assertions, and our playbook positions are different.

**Disclosure letter effect:** Read together, DL §1.1 (every fact in the data room, DD-002 to DD-012), §1.2 (public registers) and the Seller's buyer-knowledge clause 8.3 would bar claims on every known issue in the data room: Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay, the export incident, Sandbar, Mossvale and the lease. Each of these needs a specific protection (a condition, a funds-flow line, a specific indemnity or a price mechanism) rather than reliance on the general warranties.

## Material departures and reasoning

**1. General cap (cl. 12.1).** Seller: 20% / AUD 4.8m. Playbook: 25% / AUD 6m starting position. The 20% figure is a conditional fallback that needs Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft. None has been given. Reject and hold at 25%.

**2. Thresholds (cl. 12.2).** Seller: de minimis AUD 25,000, basket AUD 250,000 with recovery of the excess only. Playbook: de minimis AUD 5,000, basket AUD 50,000 with first-dollar recovery once exceeded. The Seller's basket is five times ours and works as a deductible, so the Seller would absorb roughly the first AUD 250k of losses. Reject.

**3. Time limits (cl. 12.3 / 13).** Seller: 18 months, plus a clause applying "any limitation" to all claims. Playbook: 24 months for general claims. 18 months is a fallback that needs Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given. The "applies to all Claims" wording is a hidden general-regime override, which the playbook prohibits. Reject both.

**4. Fundamental/Title (capacity and title).** Seller: same caps and time limits as general warranties. Playbook: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. This is a direct conflict with the playbook and a core issue. Reject in full.

**5. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (cl. 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5).** Seller: applies to "all Claims of any nature", which captures fraud. Playbook: fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct are carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable, and no one may waive this. Reject; the carve-out must be express.

**6. Disclosure (Schedule 7; DL §1.1-1.2).** Seller: general disclosure of the whole data room and public registers. Playbook: specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure. Reject both paragraphs.

**7. Buyer knowledge (cl. 8.3).** Seller: no claim for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records. Playbook: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier needs named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry, and can never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity. Reject. The Seller's clause is especially harmful because the known issues are all in the data room.

**8. Bluefen consent (cl. 3 / 6.3).** Seller: reasonable endeavours, with consent treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. DL §2 confirms no final consent and no evidence of conditions. Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue (about 30%). Playbook: effective consent and evidence that the conditions are satisfied before Completion, not consent-on-delivery. Reasonable endeavours is insufficient for a material customer consent. Reject; make this a condition precedent.

**9. Riverlark facility (cl. 2 / 7).** Seller: about AUD 3.2m outstanding, with a release "following Completion". DL §3 confirms it has not been repaid and no discharge is included. Playbook: current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases. A post-Completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval. Reject. The funds flow does not show a payout, which must be fixed. Since the price is debt-free and cash-free, this debt must come out of the price at Completion.

**10. Funds flow and DD-005 bonuses.** Seller: the funds flow "reflects the agreed price mechanics", and the AUD 420,000 bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised. DL §5 says the bonuses are not in the funds flow and the on-costs are unquantified. Playbook: the bonuses plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded, and the funds flow must not silently exclude them. The "agreed" claim is unverified. Reject and require a corrected funds flow.

**11. Ironquay IP (cl. 11.1).** Seller: the indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "adequate". DL §4 says DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open, which is not independent bank verification, and no payment receipt or assignment is in the data room. Playbook: broaden the narrow indemnity and preserve the SOW3 cure. The AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way, so we should not treat it as confirmed. Reject the narrow indemnity; require broader coverage of Ironquay IP and transfer of Project Materials, and independent evidence of the payment position.

**12. Export/privacy incident (cl. 4.6 / Sch 6; DL §6).** Seller: a "preliminary operational matter" that is "not expected to be material". DL §6 says about 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps) may have been sent to an unintended external address. It does not establish access, scope or notification. Playbook: preserve logs, investigate and require updates, and assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction. We should neither accept the "not material" characterisation nor assert a breach. Require log preservation, a defined investigation scope and regular written updates before signing. Obtain privacy counsel's view on whether any notification obligation applies. Any specific protection is a deal-team decision and should not be sized without instruction.

**13. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000).** Seller: "ordinary-course operating costs". DL §8 says the disclosure does not state whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable or accrued. Playbook: assess them, with no automatic Debt classification or price deduction. Do not accept the "ordinary course" label without review. Request the three contracts and check whether they are linked in timing or scope, since DD-008 and DD-011 were read together.

**14. Tax and IP.** Seller: "settled under the general regime above". Playbook: Tax and IP terms remain OPEN, with no unlimited liability assumed and no resolution. Reject. Keep these in separate categories and mark them open.

**15. Title (DL §10).** Seller: title is evidenced by the share register at DD-012. Playbook: independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence is required. DD-012 is an internal supplied source and not independent proof. Reject. Require independent evidence, such as a current ASIC company extract, a PPSR search for encumbrances (which should show Riverlark's security), and evidence of the Seller's authority to sell.

**16. Mossvale (DL §9) and office lease (DL §7).** These are not covered by the playbook. Both DL entries say the documents do not state that consent is required for the share sale. Do not assume either way. Have the assignment restriction (Mossvale) and the notification obligation (lease) reviewed to determine whether a change-of-control trigger applies, and seek a deal-team instruction on the position.

**17. Reviewer efficiency note.** Reject. It asks us to skip [STANDARD] clauses that have not been cleared.

## Recommendations (summary)

1. **Reject the "FINAL", "agreed" and "pre-cleared" framing** and treat the whole package as open, including the [STANDARD] clauses.
2. **Caps and thresholds:** 25% / AUD 6m general cap; AUD 5,000 de minimis; AUD 50,000 first-dollar basket. Do not offer the 20% / AUD 4.8m fallback without Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the draft.
3. **Time limits:** 24 months for general claims. Remove the "any limitation applies to all Claims" wording.
4. **Fundamental/Title:** separate regime with a 100% cap, at least six years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
5. **Fraud carve-out:** express, from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance. Non-waivable.
6. **Disclosure:** specific fair disclosure only. Delete the data-room and public-register deemed disclosure in Schedule 7 and DL §1.1-1.2.
7. **Buyer knowledge:** delete clause 8.3. Any qualifier needs named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry, and never excuses title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
8. **Bluefen:** condition precedent requiring effective consent and evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion.
9. **Riverlark:** payoff letter, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective releases. Any post-Completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
10. **Funds flow:** itemise the AUD 420,000 bonuses plus on-costs, or make them Seller-funded. Show the Riverlark payout.
11. **Ironquay:** broaden the indemnity, preserve the SOW3 cure, and obtain independent evidence of the AUD 180,000 position.
12. **Export incident:** preserve logs, define the investigation scope, require regular updates, and obtain privacy advice. Do not characterise it either way.
13. **Sandbar:** assess the three contracts. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
14. **Tax and IP:** keep open and separate. Do not accept "settled under the general regime".
15. **Title:** require independent evidence (ASIC extract, PPSR search, Seller authority). Treat DD-012 as internal only.
16. **Mossvale and lease:** obtain a clause review and a deal-team instruction.

This is a first-pass issues review to support the deal team. It is not a final legal opinion, and the responsible lawyer should confirm the positions before anything goes back to the Seller.
